about: Six example values profiles used only by the sample guides, so readers can see how different values change the same ballot's results. Evidence is tagged once on three value tensions; each profile weighs them (1-3) and leans toward one side. These mappings are judgment calls, shown so readers can disagree.

U.name: Universalism vs. Particularism
U.plus: Universalism: rights and duties that extend to everyone, including people outside the community or nation (open immigration, international cooperation, universal programs)
U.minus: Particularism: priority for one's own nation, state or community (border enforcement, sovereignty, local control, local preference)

E.name: Equality vs. Freedom
E.plus: Equality: collective provision, redistribution, or rules for equity and safety (public programs, progressive taxes, regulation, worker and tenant protections)
E.minus: Freedom: individual choice, lower taxes, less regulation, merit-based rules, private property

P.name: Progress vs. Order and tradition
P.plus: Progress: changing institutions and norms toward social change and reform
P.minus: Order and tradition: stability, law enforcement, faith, family, cultural continuity, incremental change

tagging: Tag each evidence row on any of U, E, P it clearly bears on: + for the first pole, - for the second, 0 if genuinely mixed; leave an axis out if the row does not bear on it. For a measure, tag what a YES vote does. Tag what the action does, not who did it; never use party.

profiles.name: Progressive Egalitarian
profiles.summary: Reduce harm and inequality through collective action; expand rights and inclusion.

profiles.name: Civic Institutionalist
profiles.summary: Protect rule of law, democratic norms and steady, evidence-based institutions; avoid radical disruption.

profiles.name: Individualist Constitutionalist
profiles.summary: Individual liberty, self-reliance, economic freedom and strict limits on government.

profiles.name: Traditionalist Moralist
profiles.summary: Moral order, faith, family and cultural continuity anchor a healthy society.

profiles.name: Populist Nationalist Producer
profiles.summary: Protect the national community, workers' livelihoods and sovereignty from elite or foreign interference.

profiles.name: Libertarian Autonomist
profiles.summary: Maximum personal freedom in social and economic life; voluntary cooperation over state coercion.
